speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Government will undertake a final environmental impact assessment study to consider the holistic impact of the Cross Island MRT Line before making a decision on which of the two existing alignment options to choose from.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The study was divided into two phases, with the first phase focusing on the environmental impact of undertaking site investigation works on the CCNR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The second phase of the study focused on the potential environmental impact of the construction and operational phases of the CRL.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Together, they would provide a complete assessment of the environmental impact of the project.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: They were gazetted in February 2016 and were widely reported in the media.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Nature Groups were also invited to observe the actual conduct of the site investigation works in the CCNR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Phase 2 of the study was conducted based on a robust set of engineering schemes, which were independently reviewed by an International Panel of Advisors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA has posted a copy of the report on its website for public viewing and feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In undertaking the EIA, LTA engaged with stakeholders for both alignments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: These included discussions and site visits with the Nature Groups as well as local grassroots leaders and residents who may be affected.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My first supplementary question is this: in assessing the impact of CRL, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether the Government has evaluated, one, the animal population projections; and two, the future impact of climate change for the critically endangered and endangered species in the CCNR and its adjacent forest, and whether this information will be made available to the public.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The basis of my supplementary question is as follows.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It has been reported in the EIA report, I believe, that various critically endangered species as well as endangered species of animals tend to be affected as a result.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, it is unclear whether the Government, whether by EIA or other studies, has tracked the population sizes of these species and, more crucially, whether there have been quantitative projections made to gauge how these population sizes may shift due to the construction.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is also unclear whether fairly established matrix used in conservation, such as species richness or species evenness, has been considered.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For the long-term impact of climate change, factoring in this aspect will allow for better understanding of the true resilience of the ecosystem in this area, which is important, given that the effects of habitat fragmentation and loss will have long-term impacts on the ecosystem in the area.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My second supplementary question is that even with mitigation, habitat loss and fragmentation at the worksite may result in the loss of ecosystem services, such as carbon sequestration and natural heritage, currently provided by these areas.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the Ministry conduct a study to holistically evaluate, if it has not, the economic, cultural and environmental value of these ecosystem services provided at these sites before making a decision on the CRL?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The rationale for me asking this supplementary question is simply that the idea is that when environmental degradation involving habitat loss and habitat fragmentation occurs, even if trees are replanted, the ecosystem services provided by the original forest may either be lost or will take decades or more to be re-established to its prior magnitude and scale.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The important principle here is that degraded ecosystems cannot be regenerated wholesale, they can only be rehabilitated.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: He has not provided a criticism of either the methodology or the process, or the experts, or the people that have been involved in the EIA.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, as far as the EIA is concerned, it is limited to the projected plans and designs of the CRL and its interaction with the Central Catchment Area.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is not designed to take a whole-of-economy or whole-of-biome approach.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Those are things that, having had the EIA, the stakeholders, the Ministry, the various agencies involved have to take into consideration, including, for example, the economic impact.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Is the Member suggesting that we redo the EIA because he fundamentally disagrees with the methodology and the findings?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Thirdly, I would just make the point that if the question is how might climate change or change in biodiversity interact with any given technical study limited to one specific part of our biome, that is a moving target.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That would be something that you can never be satisfied you have done enough because the next study, say, two or three years henceforth, the climate will have changed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These are things that academics have to continue to study even as we make our decisions about how to build our public transport system.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, perhaps, the Member might clarify what exactly he is criticising on the EIA and is he advocating for a specific choice for the CRL.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I am not criticising but I have highlighted, firstly, in my Parliamentary Question to ask the Minister whether the Government undertake a final EIA study to consider the holistic impact.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I believe I have also touched on and explained, for my first supplementary question, about the animal population projection and the future impact of climate change.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: If this has been done, and if the Senior Minister of State, the Ministry, is satisfied, so be it.
